meaning: to argue against an idea on purpose in order to test how strong it is
literal_translation: karşıt bir görüşü bilerek savunmak (fikrin sağlamlığını test etmek için)
example: I don't fully agree with the plan, but I'll play devil's advocate to see if it holds up.
origin: From the Catholic Church's role of an official who argued against a candidate's sainthood to test the case

wrong_meanings.meaning: to pretend to be evil in a story
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about arguing a position in discussion, not about acting evil.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to refuse to give any opinion at all
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: Playing devil's advocate means giving a strong opposing opinion, not staying silent.

wrong_meanings.meaning: to agree with everyone in a meeting
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which means challenging the group's view.

explanation: 'Play devil's advocate' means to take the opposite side of an argument on purpose, so that an idea is examined more carefully. It is useful when giving and supporting an opinion in a discussion.
